messages:
laura_sales: FYI - AcmeCorp POC is blocked. PrivateLink endpoint works in some AZs but TLS handshakes fail for requests coming through their network firewall. They see 525/SSL handshake in their logs. customer says: "works from bastion but not app subnets"

devon_se: Thanks Laura. Can you paste the curl/openssl output and the resolver config they use? suspect split-horizon DNS or firewall rewriting SNI.

laura_sales: Pasting what they sent (redacted IPs):

```
$ curl -v https://private.redwood-acme.internal -o /dev/null
* Connected to 10.10.18.5 (10.10.18.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake starts
* TLS handshake error: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to 10.10.18.5:443
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL connect error
```

and openssl from their app host:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.10.18.5:443 -servername private.redwood-acme.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
139704...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:s3_srvr.c:xxxxx
140704...:error:1409E0E5:SSL routines:ssl3_write_pending:bad write retry:s3_pkt.c:xxxx
```

laura_sales: They also said their firewall vendor does TLS termination/inspection in some SPs and rewrites SNI. They haven't opened outbound to ocsp/live CRL endpoints yet.

anjali_engineer: OK — a few possible culprits: split-horizon DNS returning private ENI IPs, firewall doing TLS intercept and not forwarding original SNI, or OCSP/CRL egress blocked causing handshake stalls if stapling expected. Also if the firewall rewrites SNI to the external hostname, cert CN mismatch can trigger immediate failure.

anjali_engineer: Can we confirm what hostname the cert uses on the private endpoint? Devon, do we have the cert chain shown for the private endpoints (internal SANs)?

devon_se: Yes, private endpoints present a cert with SANs: private.redwood-acme.internal, *.redwood-internal, and a customer-verified SAN for the private domain. OCSP stapling is enabled by default. I'll upload the cert chain to the ticket.

nate_sre: Quick checks for them to run from an affected app host:

```
# 1) dig against the resolver
dig +short private.redwood-acme.internal @169.254.169.253

# 2) check SNI seen by endpoint (tcpdump on endpoint ENI)
tcpdump -nni any 'tcp port 443' -A | grep -i 'private.redwood-acme.internal' || true

# 3) curl with --resolve to bypass DNS and test hostname vs IP
curl -v --resolve private.redwood-acme.internal:443:10.10.18.5 https://private.redwood-acme.internal/

# 4) test OCSP access
curl -v https://ocsp.example-ca.com/status | head
```

nate_sre: Also ask them to try `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.18.5:443 -servername private.redwood-acme.internal -status` to see OCSP stapling details.

laura_sales: I sent the commands. Their reply: dig resolves to the private ENI IP; tcpdump on our side shows ClientHello with SNI=public.redwood.com (their firewall rewrote it) and no OCSP stapled response.

anjali_engineer: That matches SNI rewrite. If their firewall substitutes SNI, the endpoint's cert SAN won't match -> handshake abort. Two mitigation paths: 1) Have their firewall do TLS passthrough for this traffic (recommended). 2) If inspection is required, configure the firewall to preserve original SNI or configure a cert on the firewall with a SAN that includes the private domain (not ideal). Also need to ensure outbound access to our CA OCSP/CRL endpoints so stapling can succeed.

devon_se: For a faster workaround, we can enable a fallback policy on the Private endpoint to accept the rewritten SNI if it maps to an allowed CN we control, but that requires a short config change and has security implications. Would need sales/legal ok.

laura_sales: Customer asked about timeline and whether this is considered an enterprise blocker. What's the effort for the fallback?

anjali_engineer: Engineering estimate: ~2 dev-days to add optional SNI-accept-list for Private endpoints, + 1 day for config rollout and tests. Risk: makes SNI validation looser. Prefer to avoid for POC.

nate_sre: Meanwhile, operationally we can advise their network team to: allow outbound to ocsp.* and crl.* for our CA IP ranges, configure firewall to bypass TLS inspection for the endpoint CIDR, or set DNS so app hosts resolve to bastion/proxy that can do mutual TLS with the firewall.

laura_sales: They've agreed to try bypassing inspection for the POC and open OCSP egress. I'll update once they test. If they can't change firewall rules, they'll ask for the fallback route.

devon_se: Please collect a packet capture from their app host showing ClientHello before and after firewall. If they can't share PCAP, a `hexdump` of the TLS ClientHello is enough. We need evidence to support SNI rewrite claim.

laura_sales: Got it. Thanks all. looping in infra-bot to add a private task. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Task created: #POC-1993456789 - Investigate SNI rewrite/OCSP egress for AcmeCorp POC. Assignee: devon_se. ETA: 2d.

devon_se: I'll start the cert-chain review today and prepare the opt-in fallback plan doc.

laura_sales: Update at 18:02 their network team confirmed bypass and opened ocsp endpoints. They report TLS handshakes now succeed from app hosts. Customer will validate end-to-end tomorrow. :relieved:

anjali_engineer: Great. If they hit flaky stalls, we should check for CRL timeouts and retry/backoff in our TLS stack. Could also enable short-term verbose logs around OCSP retrieval on the endpoint.

laura_sales: Closing for now, keeping task open until customer sign-off. Thanks everyone. :party:
